acceptanceCriteria: `queue status` and `plan preview` read no receipt below the retained checkpoint when one is usable, proved by a test that counts receipt reads.
A checkpoint read returns the same selected records, sequence and head binding as the complete audit, and any unusable checkpoint or unsettled journal yields exactly the complete audit's answer.
Reads never create, replace or delete the checkpoint; `receipt audit` and every writer keep the complete audit.
Measured before/after wall time on the live store is retained in the build log, with the checkpoint read's detection limits stated in the spec.
body:
## Problem

GitHub issue beamfall/corvint#446. `queue status` and `plan preview` replay the whole receipt chain on every call. On this store at 1,829 receipts a build of origin/main e5d96823 took 4.5-4.9 s for `queue status` (three complete audits plus an attempt inventory scan); the issue reports 9-22 s at about 1,350 receipts under load. The cost grows with history and widens the window in which a concurrent writer moves the snapshot.

## Change

1. One memoized journal audit per read command; projections reuse the capture's intent digests.
2. A writer-retained derived checkpoint (`taskman-audit-checkpoint/0`, sibling of the state directory). Reads rebind it to its receipt, walk only later receipts with the unchanged validators, verify every projection, and fall back to the complete audit on any doubt. `receipt audit` and every writer stay complete.

Spec: CAL-V0-059..061 in docs/specs/corvint-tasks-agent-leases-v0.md.

Read-only independent verification (Codex batch B) plus mechanical check of cited commits, tests and paths; no suite rerun for this closure.

title: corvint-tasks: queue status and plan preview cost scales with receipt history (GitHub 446)
